source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text:
Comparing traditional transplanting (uprooting and replanting seedlings) with sowing rice in rows using a hand-pulled drum seeder: transplanting requires nursery management and heavy manual labor to replant seedlings one by one, while the drum seeder sows pre-germinated seed directly into rows in one pass across the leveled, puddled field. Ordinary broadcasting scatters seed unevenly (heavier where the sower stood, thin elsewhere) and is harder to weed because the rice is not in rows; drum-seeded rice instead grows in straight, evenly spaced rows similar to transplanted rice, and is easier to weed because the rows can be told apart from weeds. Compared with ordinary broadcasting, the drum seeder places seed at a controlled depth so seedlings establish more evenly.

Overall stated benefits: reduced seed rate, better and more even germination, lower labor cost than transplanting, straight planting rows that help with fertilizer application and weeding, and a shorter turnaround than transplanting since there is no separate nursery stage.
